questions.q: What does the code review confirm about isUserInGroup's GlideRecord usage, per Chapter 3's performance lessons?
options: Its membership query uses setLimit(1) and neither query runs inside a loop
It queries every table on the instance to find a match
It runs the same GlideRecord query twice for safety
It avoids GlideRecord entirely in favor of a hardcoded list
questions.explain: setLimit(1) stops the query at the first match, and both queries run exactly once per call -- neither sits inside a loop.

options: Loose equality could match other truthy-looking values in ways that mask a bug, where strict equality only matches the exact string "true"
== is slower to execute than === in every case
GlideAjax never returns the string "true" at all
This comparison would cause a syntax error
questions.explain: GlideAjax answers always arrive as strings, so the review prefers answer === 'true' -- an exact match -- over the looser == comparison.

questions.q: Why does getReferenceDisplayValue only call gs.info() on the path where isValidField(fieldName) fails, and not on every successful call?
options: A diagnostic log reserved for an abnormal case stays useful; logging every routine successful call would flood the system log and bury the messages that matter
gs.info() can only be called once per Script Include
Logging on success would cause the method to return the wrong value
ServiceNow disables gs.info() calls inside Script Includes by default
questions.explain: This matches Chapter 6's logging guidance: log the abnormal case developers need to see, not routine successful calls that just add noise.

options: GlideRecord field values always come back as strings, so a strict comparison needs a matching string on the other side
Priority is always a Boolean field on the task table
Using the number 1 would throw a runtime error
current.getValue() only works when compared against strings by platform rule
questions.explain: getValue() returns a GlideRecord field's raw value as a string, so === '1' correctly matches it; === 1 (a number) would never be true.

questions.q: What is this course's next step in the ServiceNow Administrator to Technical Architect path, according to this lesson?
options: ServiceNow Scripting & Application Development, which builds full scoped applications on top of these same low-level skills
A repeat of this same JavaScript course at a deeper level
A course unrelated to ServiceNow development
There is no next course -- this is the final course in the path
questions.explain: This course stayed deliberately low-level; the next course applies these skills to building full scoped applications -- tables, UI policies, workflows, and reusable Script Includes.
